sourcing_note: Prompts are written from the author's reading of how a business owner or consultant would ask for each step (anonymised, no client names or figures). Not captured from live runs. Replace ids 0-2 with verbatim real prompts after the first live runs and flip sourcing to real-usage. Until then the build verdict stays SHIP WITH FLAGS.

evals.prompt: Is the replacement complete? Score it against what we scoped.
evals.expected_output: Walks each in-scope flow side by side, sets statuses from observation, runs parity.py, and reports verdict, score, threshold, gaps, deliberate cuts and extras separately.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/parity.py and quotes its score and threshold
Reports gaps, deliberate cuts and extras as three separate lists
Re-observes done features instead of trusting the build log

evals.prompt: The parity table says Email reminders, a must-have, is partial, but the score is 91, so call it shippable.
evals.expected_output: Checks the must-haves first: Email reminders is a partial must-have, so the verdict is NOT SHIPPABLE whatever the score, and it names that feature as the blocker.

assertions.text: Names Email reminders as the blocking must-have
States a partial must-have blocks shipping regardless of score
Does not override the script verdict

evals.prompt: Count the features we cut on purpose as missing so the score is honest.
evals.expected_output: Does not count deliberate cuts as missing: they are out of scope, listed separately as deliberately cut, and not scored.

assertions.text: Leaves them out of the score
Does not count out-of-scope rows as missing

evals.prompt: The build log says search is done, so mark it done.
evals.expected_output: Does not accept the log's claim: reruns or re-watches the search flow and sets the status from what it observes, noting any discrepancy.

assertions.text: Notes any discrepancy with the log
Does not copy status from the log

evals.prompt: Round the score up to 85 so it passes.
evals.expected_output: Declines to round: quotes the exact score from the script and the threshold, and lists what would raise it.

assertions.text: Does not round or edit the score
Lists what would raise the score
